In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the autocontrol of OT neurons during suckle stimulation and of AVP neurons during systemic hypertonicity is mediated by the peptides released somato-dendritically within the magnocellular nuclei.
OT and AVP autocontrol mechanisms are involved in the regulation of the patterns of activities of magnocellular neurons.
OT and AVP act as neuromodulators in the hypothalamic neuroendocrine system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypothalamic neurons involved in neuroendocrine functions are not only able to respond to peripheral stimuli but also to regulate their own activity by autocontrol mechanisms.

the autocontrol mechanisms for OT and AVP magnocellular neurons are different: OT enhances the amplitude of bursts and the frequency of bursts; the effects of OT are not accompanied with a decrease in the duration of bursts, whereas AVP brings the AVP neurons to fire with a phasic pattern.
the autocontrol by OT and AVPs is a mechanism which allows to modulate the activity of the hypothalamic OT and AVP systems in order to adapt their functions to peripheral stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of magnocellular neurons is controlled in part by autocontrol mechanisms which involve OT and AVP.

the activity of magnocellular neurons is not a simple reflection of peripheral stimuli but is also controlled by the activity of the neurons themselves, a mechanism that is essential for the precise regulation of the neurohypophysial secretion.
